# coffee_machine_0

Built from the eight supplied photos, without network access. The references show a white/chrome capsule coffee machine with a hinged extraction head and a right steam tower. They do **not** show a bean hopper or a conventional installed espresso portafilter. Photo appearance takes precedence: no hopper was invented. The ambiguous handled item on the right tray is represented as the requested separate removable portafilter approximation; that identification, bowl interior and handle shape are uncertain.

## Files and frame

`model.blend` and Y-up `model.glb` contain ten separately named physical/visual parts, procedural geometry and PBR materials. `parts/*.obj` use metres, +Z up, in the common object frame at the closed default pose. Origin is the supplied bottom-centre frame. +X points out of the front; +Y points to the machine's right. The resulting bounds are about **0.280 × 0.256 × 0.399 m**, versus the supplied visible-surface reconstruction estimate of 0.270 × 0.241 × 0.390 m. Rear depth, local protrusions and shell radii were inferred from the photographs. No extra metric measurement was made.

Run `~/blender/blender -b -P build.py`. The build also regenerates review and validation through the included `review.py` and `validate.py` helpers. The review compositor uses the local system Python/Pillow; validation uses Blender's NumPy. The saved Blender scene includes the studio and source-camera rig; GLB contains only the asset. The roughness PNG is embedded in GLB and retained under `textures/`. Branding is recreated as shallow raised geometry, not a photo texture. No generated imagery was used.

## Motion

- **Drip tray:** separate part, prismatic travel 0–0.12 m along +X. Cup support rides with it in the coarse physics assembly, though its mesh is separately removable. Set the `drip_tray_joint` empty's X location to exercise it in Blender.
- **Portafilter approximation:** separate free body, initially resting on the tray. It is not constrained to the machine. A grasp/removal simulation should detach it from any enclosing asset root.
- **Brew head:** added because the photos demonstrate it. Frames 1/100 are closed and frame 50 is open. The observed lifting mechanism is approximated by a virtual rear hinge and a coupled pair of rigid support links. It is not a measured linkage reconstruction. Intermediate motion and self-collision are not mechanically validated.
- Locking lever rides with the head. Tank, tank lid and steam wand are separately meshed fixed attachments for the supplied coarse physics assembly. Their real removal/swivel mechanisms were not measured. Joint axes/origins/ranges and attachment mapping are in `model.json`; distances use metres and angles use radians. glTF animation illustrates head motion, not physics constraints.

## Contact geometry and physical assumptions

Eight numbered OBJ proxies are closed convex solids, in the same +Z-up object frame as the part exports. They deliberately omit small vents and grating holes. Their thin-axis dimensions are at least 14 mm; none is a thin shell. `validation.json` records manifold-edge, convexity, bounds and positive-volume checks.

| Proxy | Owner / intended contacts |
|---|---|
| 0 | Chassis underside and counter support |
| 1 | Rear fixed housing, including fixed reservoir envelope |
| 2 | Main brew column and group collar envelope |
| 3 | Movable brew-head envelope, transformed about its joint |
| 4 | Sliding drip tray support envelope |
| 5 | Circular cup support, attached to tray; square envelope |
| 6 | Removable portafilter including handle; coarse single envelope |
| 7 | Fixed wand envelope; fills the space inside its curved shape |

The support links have no independent collision proxy. Proxies for attached parts should be grouped into their owning rigid body, and collisions between fixed attachments disabled. Broad envelopes overlap inside the machine, overfill cavities, and can obstruct close finger/cup interactions: they are suitable for coarse rigid-body contacts, not precise insertion or capsule handling. Mesh exteriors include thin decorative details; **collision** geometry supplies the minimum thickness constraint.

Assumed total mass: 6.5 kg. Effective bulk density guess: 650 kg/m³, accounting for hollow construction; it is not the material density of steel. Mass fractions sum to one. Friction 0.5 and restitution 0.05 are starting guesses. No mass, centre of mass, inertia, friction, joint effort or damping was measured. A downstream simulator must compute inertia from chosen masses/proxies and configure its solver. No fluid, thermal, electrical, capsule extraction or brewing physics is included.

## Camera review and limitations

`review.jpg` shows all five calibrated source crops next to their renders, composited over grey. The exact supplied OpenCV camera transforms and K matrices are used; renders are at 70% resolution with equivalent intrinsics. `view_0` uses the open head; the other views use the closed head. In-hand images informed shape but have no known camera and are not presented as calibrated comparisons.

`evaluation.json` reports raw alpha-versus-mask IoU. These are **not** unoccluded silhouette accuracy claims. `view_2` contains a large hand occlusion; `view_3`'s supplied mask omits much of the clearly visible head and tower, making its raw score unsuitable for geometry assessment. The target IoU >0.85 was not established across all views. Reliable cropped views and the open-head view are approximately 0.91, 0.85 and 0.84, respectively; see the generated file for final exact values.

The render iterations corrected parenting, open-head placement, tray roundness, cup-support position and lighting. Remaining mismatches include the extraction-head linkage/interior, the rear shell/tank profile, exact chrome reflections, wand curvature, embossed text curvature and the uncertain portafilter. Chrome is lit by a simple studio with reflection cards, not the captured kitchen. Rear/bottom details are inferred, not reconstructed.

This is an **offline procedural asset reconstruction**, not real-time online estimation. `build_report.json` records actual wall time for the final build/export/five-render pass and mesh triangle count; that time excludes interactive authoring, review compositing and validation. No camera trajectory, source timestamps or capture video was supplied, so no synchronized scene replay or online timing claim is made. No website was published. Outputs stay in the explicitly requested object folder.

## Connection audit revision

The source model and simulation-rest instance metadata are part of the [connection audit](../../connection_audit/notes.md). This is not a blanket physics or photo-fit pass. Native contact measurements, failed release trials, source-photo coverage and accepted/rejected pose proposals are recorded there.

Contact geometry uses the authored MJCF convex pieces; open vessels retain separate floors and wall pieces in the revised assembly. Triangle meshes describe the visible surfaces. Source mass, explicit inertia and friction values are priors, not physical measurements. Any retained web3 hold is a display/release policy, not evidence that the asset is supported. Capture poses are retained separately from corrected simulation-rest poses.
